stories.delivered_paragraph: The Federal Communications Commission says it will bar imports of “advanced robotic devices” and power inverters made abroad, covering mobile robots including humanoid and quadruped models. The measure could reshape equipment choices for U.S. robotics and solar-energy companies.

stories.delivered_paragraph: President Trump and the Justice Department separately asked the Supreme Court to overturn the $83.3 million defamation verdict won by writer E. Jean Carroll. Trump’s lawyers argue his 2019 denials of Carroll’s sexual-assault allegation were protected official presidential acts under the court’s 2024 immunity ruling, while Carroll’s case concerns statements made from the White House. The appeal asks the justices to clarify how far presidential immunity extends to public communications and could erase a major civil judgment against Trump.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The Senate voted 86-12 to advance a Russia and Iran sanctions bill that would impose 100% secondary tariffs on countries buying Russian oil and gas. The procedural vote followed a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and a remembrance for the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, who had championed the bill with Sen. Richard Blumenthal. The lopsided margin could speed final passage, putting renewed pressure on Russia’s energy customers and its sanctions-evasion tanker network.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Iran fired multiple ballistic missiles toward a U.S. base in Jordan on Tuesday, its first such attack since President Trump paused strikes against Iran on Friday, U.S. Central Command said. The attack directly tests the short diplomatic window Trump said he was giving Tehran before considering renewed military action.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Ariana Grande sued unidentified hackers in Los Angeles County Superior Court, alleging they stole and leaked unreleased songs, videos, recording material and photographs. The filing says 45 unreleased songs were hacked and leaked in 2023 alone, with hundreds of similar leaks since her 2011 debut; it seeks to identify up to 100 defendants accused of selling or posting the material online. The case could expose the networks behind entertainment leaks and seek to stop further distribution of her unfinished work.
